title: Prevent Distraction with Identity Pacts
coreMove: Choose a concrete identity that makes the planned behavior feel like proof of who you are, not a rule you are enduring.
sourcePressure: The chapter treats identity pacts as a different reinforcement mechanism, tying follow-through to a chosen identity proved through action.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would drift into affirmations instead of tying identity to repeated visible behavior.

hook: Prevent Distraction with Identity Pacts as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: volunteer trail steward maintaining weekly bridge checks
exampleSpecs.audience: steward tempted to skip reports after muddy hikes
exampleSpecs.stakes: trail safety depends on the kind of steward who documents damage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she says 'I am a steward who leaves a usable record' and uploads the bridge photo before changing boots
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A splintered bridge plank photo sits beside a mud scraper.

exampleSpecs.domain: sourdough microbakery owner protecting test-bake notes
exampleSpecs.audience: baker who sees herself as instinctive and skips records
exampleSpecs.stakes: repeatable loaves require the identity of a craftsperson who records
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, instinct excuses drift; after, she signs the test sheet as 'record-keeping baker' and logs the crumb
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A sliced test loaf rests beside a crumb-record sheet.

exampleSpecs.audience: mechanic who hates tablets but values rider safety
exampleSpecs.stakes: unclosed tickets make broken bikes look available
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he names himself a safety mechanic and closes three tickets before leaving the rack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A brake-pad gauge sits beside a maintenance tablet.

exampleSpecs.audience: translator who puts prep off until court morning
exampleSpecs.stakes: accurate testimony depends on prepared terminology
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes 'prepared interpreter' at the top of the glossary and completes the first ten terms
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A bilingual glossary card rests on a courthouse bench schedule.

exampleSpecs.domain: community garden treasurer reconciling plot fees
exampleSpecs.audience: volunteer who avoids money tasks because gardeners are communal
exampleSpecs.stakes: the garden loses fairness when fees stay vague
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he adopts the identity of transparent steward and posts the reconciled fee sheet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A seed packet tin sits beside a plot-fee ledger.

exampleSpecs.audience: narrator tempted to wing difficult names
exampleSpecs.stakes: one mispronounced name breaks listener trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she calls herself a prepared narrator and records the pronunciation list before the first take
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A pronunciation list lies beside a pop filter.
